title: Art and literature
subtitle: the arts, a still life, a bestseller with a good plot
summary: Talk about the branches of the arts, name types of painting and artist, and review a novel like a critic.

lesson.heading: The branches of the arts
rows: novels, short stories, biographies, drama, poetry
theatre, dance, cinema, ballet, opera, concerts (classical, rock, country and western)
painting, sculpture, architecture, ceramics (making pots, bowls and so on)
lesson.note: **The arts** (plural) covers all of these. **Art** (singular, uncountable) usually means fine art.

lesson.heading: art, the arts, artistic
lesson.text: **Art** can also mean creative ability or technique. A **work of art** (plural **works of art**) is an object made by a skilled artist - a painting, a drawing or a statue. **Arts and crafts** are objects such as decorations, jewellery and furniture made by hand.

examples.text: Have you read the **arts** page in the paper today?
examples.note: the part of the paper dealing with books, films, music, galleries

examples.text: Shakespeare was skilled in **the art of** poetry.
Ask Sara to help you decorate your room - she's very **artistic**.
examples.note: = shows skill and imagination in creating things

examples.text: I saw some interesting abstract **works of art** at the City Gallery.

lesson.heading: The artist, the action and the art form
Types of painting
rows: a painting of a scene in the countryside
a painting of objects that do not move, usually fruit or flowers
shapes and colours rather than images of real people or things
the painting the artist made, not a copy
a copy of a famous painting, cheap enough to hang at home

lesson.heading: Writing and publishing
lesson.text: Lisa O'Donnell is a popular **novelist**. She has written a **series** of romantic novels with a historical **setting**. They have all been **bestsellers**, although the **critics** complain that her **plots** are predictable and her **characters** are not very realistic.

examples.text: A **novel** is typically at least 150 pages long; anything shorter is a **short story**.
Her cousin is a more **literary** writer and gets better **reviews**.
Both novels will be ready for **publication** later this year.
They will also be available to download as **ebooks**.
The author read a short **extract** from the first chapter.
examples.note: an extract is a part chosen for an article or for discussion

lesson.heading: Talking about a book
lesson.text: The **plot** is the story; the **characters** are the people in it; the **setting** is the background it takes place in; the **opening passage** is the first short piece of text.

examples.text: The novel has a very interesting **plot** with some unexpected twists in it.
You know from the first page that the two main **characters** are going to fall in love.
I prefer books with a modern **setting** rather than ones about some unfamiliar period.
Max hopes his first novel will become a **bestseller**.

lesson.text: Keep the pairs straight: *sculptor* makes *sculpture*, *potter* makes *pottery*, *architect* makes *architecture*. The person ends in *-or*, *-er* or *-ect*; the art form does not.

exercises.prompt: Which branch of the arts is each person talking about?

pairs.left: 'He's created some beautiful vases, but I'm not so keen on his other pieces.'
'It doesn't have to rhyme to be good.'
'Oils to me don't have the delicacy of watercolours.'
'Her design for the new city hall won an award.'
'The first chapter was boring but it got better later.'

exercises.prompt: What type of painting is each of these?

pairs.left: a painting of the artist's mother
a bowl of fruit and some flowers on a table
coloured squares and lines, with nothing you can recognise
green hills, a river and a distant farm

exercises.prompt: Someone who makes statues is a ___.
exercises.explanation: The person is a sculptor; sculpture is the art form.

exercises.prompt: The Dutch artist Rembrandt was a master of ___ of portrait painting.
exercises.explanation: The art of + noun means the creative ability or technique of doing something.

exercises.prompt: On Saturdays there's a market in the city square where they sell all sorts of ___.
exercises.explanation: Arts and crafts is a fixed phrase: both words are plural.

exercises.prompt: Is each word the person or the art form?
The ___ have generally been very positive about Kelly's latest novel.
exercises.hint: (one word, plural - people who give their opinion of books)
exercises.explanation: Critics review books, films and music for a living. What they write are reviews.

exercises.prompt: Do you like this picture? It's only a ___. I could never afford an original.
exercises.explanation: A reproduction is a copy; the original is the painting the artist actually made.

exercises.prompt: The author began his talk by reading a short ___ from his latest book.
exercises.explanation: An extract is a part of a book chosen to be read out or discussed.

exercises.prompt: I usually prefer to read books with a modern ___ rather than ones about some unfamiliar period.
exercises.explanation: The setting is the background - the time and place - of a story.

exercises.prompt: Max is, of course, hoping that his first novel will become a ___.
exercises.hint: (one word - a book that sells in huge numbers)
exercises.explanation: A bestseller is a very popular book that sells in large numbers.

exercises.prompt: The novel has a very interesting ___ with some unexpected twists in it.
exercises.explanation: The plot is the story; the characters are the people in it.

exercises.statement: Maria's first novel is due for publication this summer, and it will also be available as an ebook.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Publication is making a book available in printed form; an ebook is the electronic version.
